question: Are C9orf72 Total FluoroSpot responses different in ALS vs HC?
method: Two-tailed Mann-Whitney U on per-donor response magnitude
finding: C9orf72 Total responses are higher in ALS (median 6720 vs 1142, p=0.00159, rank-biserial r=-0.49).

question: Are C9orf72 IFNg FluoroSpot responses different in ALS vs HC?
method: Two-tailed Mann-Whitney U on per-donor response magnitude
finding: C9orf72 IFNg responses are higher in ALS (median 2185 vs 627, p=0.0381, rank-biserial r=-0.33).

question: Are C9orf72 IL-5 FluoroSpot responses different in ALS vs HC?
method: Two-tailed Mann-Whitney U on per-donor response magnitude
finding: C9orf72 IL-5 responses are higher in ALS (median 2330 vs 208, p=0.000318, rank-biserial r=-0.56).

question: Are C9orf72 IL-10 FluoroSpot responses different in ALS vs HC?
method: Two-tailed Mann-Whitney U on per-donor response magnitude
finding: C9orf72 IL-10 responses are higher in ALS (median 1029 vs 177, p=0.00469, rank-biserial r=-0.44).

question: Do ALS responses show an IL-5/IL-10 (Th2/regulatory) bias over IFNg?
method: Two-tailed Mann-Whitney U on the per-donor IFNg/IL-5 ratio
finding: The IFNg/IL-5 ratio is lower in ALS (median 0.65) than HC (median 1.26), p=0.0483: an IL-5-biased response in ALS.
reproduces: ALS responses enriched for IL-5/IL-10 over IFNg (Fig. 2, ED Fig. 2)

question: Is the ALS Total C9orf72 response specific vs PD and AD controls?
method: Pairwise two-tailed Mann-Whitney U, ALS vs each control group
finding: ALS Total C9orf72 responses differ from HC (p<0.05) and not from PD, AD: elevated versus healthy controls but not statistically distinguished from the other neurodegenerative groups.
reproduces: C9orf72 responses elevated in disease groups vs HC (ED Fig. 2)

question: Do C9orf72 mutation carriers show stronger Total C9orf72 responses?
method: Two-tailed Mann-Whitney U, C9orf72-mutation vs no-mutation donors
finding: C9orf72-mutation carriers have Total responses with median 7263 vs 100 in non-carriers (p=0.0281).
reproduces: Mutation carriers show stronger C9orf72-specific responses (Fig. 4)

question: Is the IL-10 C9orf72 response associated with predicted survival?
method: Two-tailed Mann-Whitney U, long vs short predicted-survival donors
finding: IL-10 responses are higher in long-survival donors (median 1153 vs 100, p=0.0382).
reproduces: IL-10-mediated responses associate with longer predicted survival (Fig. 4)

question: Is predicted HLA-II binding breadth associated with observed immunogenicity?
method: Spearman correlation of predicted-HLA-bound count vs response frequency across 95 peptides
finding: Predicted HLA-II binding breadth correlates with observed response frequency (Spearman rho=0.29, p=0.00385, n=95).
reproduces: Immunogenicity associated with HLA binding (ED Fig. 5)

question: Are C9orf72-reactive T cells predominantly CD4+?
method: Mann-Whitney of CD4 vs CD8 frequency among reactive cells, per group
finding: C9orf72-reactive T cells are predominantly CD4+ HC: CD4 median 83% vs CD8 9% (p=3.4e-06); ALS: CD4 median 92% vs CD8 5% (p=3.4e-06)
reproduces: Responses predominantly CD4+ T-cell mediated (Fig. 2, ED Fig. 4)
